title: tcspecial configuration
description: The shape of a configuration: which sections there are, what an entry may say, and which words are words. Not whether it can be flown -- which attributes a node of a given type must state, whether two payloads claim one socket, whether a link arrives by a name its far end lists are rules about meaning, tested against real buses, and tcsverify is the one place they live. A file this accepts may still be refused, and the refusal will say why.

destination.description: One line out of a node: the node it reaches and the name it arrives there by, separated by a dot, `gateway.readings`. The name is one the node it reaches lists under the sink the line arrives at.

arrival.description: A name a line may arrive at one of a node's data sinks by: one word, with no dot in it.

gateway.description: What this node is called, unique across the configuration: the first key of the node, the word for a node of the section and the name after it.

group.description: The payload group that reads it, where it is in one. Optional, though a payload that states a trigger needs one: the interval of its group is how often it is asked.

world-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `world-out`: each the node it reaches and the name it arrives by, `node.name`, alone or in a list.

moc-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `moc-out`: each the node it reaches and the name it arrives by, `node.name`, alone or in a list.

world-in.description: The names a groundward line may arrive at this node's `world-in` by, which a link to it names after the dot. A vote's world-in names are its inputs.

moc-in.description: The names a vehicleward line may arrive at this node's `moc-in` by, which a link to it names after the dot. A vote's world-in names are its inputs.

ground_base.description: Where the ground station is, as address:port. What each node linked into this gateway node produces is sent to that address, at that port plus the node's device id.

bridge_base.description: Where the F´ bridge component is, as address:port: a gateway_fprime node's ground_base. What each node linked into it produces is sent to that address, at that port plus the node's device id.

apid_base.description: The APID, 0 to 0x7FF, of the CCSDS telecommands the ground sends a gateway_yamcs node: what each node linked into it produces goes to the ground as CCSDS telemetry under this APID plus its own device id. Decimal, or hexadecimal with 0x.

fprime_id_base.description: The first of the F´ IDs the bridge gives what arrives at a gateway_fprime node: each node linked into it is this ID plus its own device id. Decimal, or hexadecimal with 0x.

cmd_msgid.description: The message ID what a gateway_cfs node sends on is published under on the cFS software bus: a command's, with 0x80 set. Required where a line or a command binding leaves the node.

tlm_base.description: The first of the message IDs what arrives at a gateway_cfs node is published under: each node linked into it is this plus its own device id.

ip_protocol.description: The IP protocol number a node reached with `protocol: raw` reads and writes, 1 to 254. For a raw socket and nothing else.

sends_from.description: Where a datagram payload that speaks first sends from -- a host and a port over udp, as 10.0.0.7:7001, or a path over unix_dgram -- and so the one address it is read from: anything else that reaches the vehicle's socket is turned away and counted. Optional; without it the payload is learnt from the first datagram that arrives. Not on a payload that is asked or only driven, which is reached at its address.

sim_address.description: Where an hdlc, spi, rpmsg, iio, i2c_tmass or spi_tmass payload is reached over UDP when it is simulated, as a loopback address and port: 127.0.0.1:7950. Used under --simulate=some or all, and not under none, the flight setting, when the device is opened.

trigger_interval.description: How often the trigger goes out, as a length of time: how often this payload is asked. For a payload that states a trigger and is in no group -- a payload in one is asked when its group is read. A payload with no trigger has nothing to send, and states `poll_interval` instead.

poll_interval.description: The least time between issuing one read of this node and issuing the next, as a length of time: a floor on the reading of a part nothing asks, not a cadence -- there is no telling how soon a descriptor will have anything, and what the interval prevents is reading again immediately for an answer already given. For a node in no group, and never beside a `trigger` -- a node that is asked is read because it was asked, which is `trigger_interval`.

read_delay.description: How long to wait between sending the trigger and reading the answer, as a length of time: what the part's interface document says it takes to answer. With one, a pass asks, waits and reads the answer to the question it just asked; with none, a pass reads what the last ask produced and asks again, so the reading is one interval old. Only beside a `trigger`.

init.description: What to write to this payload as the vehicle opens it -- at startup, and whenever the ground starts it again -- written as a trigger is: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. A write that fails stops the node from starting. Not on lines that are watched, a sensor's sample buffer, or a datagram payload that speaks first.

trigger.description: What to write to make this payload answer: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. A payload that states one is asked and is read at the interval of the payload group it is in; one that states none is only read, and a line delivering into it is refused. A payload says what asks it or that it sends on its own, never both, and there is no mode attribute: which it is follows from whether it has a trigger.

terminators.description: The byte sequences that each end a packet of a stream -- a line, or a tcp or unix_stream socket -- where the first of them arrives whole, which is the packet's last bytes. A list, one entry per terminator, each written as a trigger is: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. Not beside a length_prefix.

length_prefix.description: What a packet's first bytes say its length is, counting the bytes after them: u8, or u16be or u16le for two bytes with the more or the less significant first. The packet is delivered prefix and all. Needs a read_timeout, which may be none, and is not beside terminators.

state_interval.description: How often to report what a set of discrete lines is, as a length of time: 5 s. Events say when a line changed and this says what the lines are, so a payload may ask for either or both. It exists for the two things edges cannot do: a line that has not changed since the vehicle started tells the ground nothing, and the kernel's event queue is finite, so a burst can leave the ground holding a value that is wrong. Inputs only.

age.description: For a `vote`: how old a reading may be and still be voted on, as a length of time: `2 s`. Older ones are left out. Unstated, a reading stands until it is replaced.

unit.description: The unit the node's values are in: K, V, A, W, m, m/s, N, kg/s or ratio. Required of a `to_value` conversion and of a `process` computation, whose answers are numbers of it.

executable.description: The program this node runs: an app node's application, or the program a `process` computation runs on what arrives. Executed with a leading `~` and `$HOME` expanded as a shell would expand them -- to the home directory and to the value of the environment variable HOME, of whatever runs it. An app node's is run with the node's name as its first argument.

gatewaysType.description: The key an entry of the section groups its nodes by: the word type, one space, and the configuration's own word for the type, which is every node's under it. A link to the ground over the radio is gateway_radio; one to a Yamcs ground station is gateway_yamcs; one to an F´ bridge component is gateway_fprime; one to a cFS software bus is gateway_cfs. The order of the entries, and of the nodes under each, means nothing.

group.description: The payload group that reads it, where it is in one. Optional, though a payload that states a trigger needs one: the interval of its group is how often it is asked.

app-payload-arg.description: What an app node's program is told about the payload stream, as the argument after the node's name. Said by the kinds that handle payload data -- app_payload_veh, app_all_veh, app_pl, app_all_pl -- and required of them, the arguments being a fixed list.

app-gateway-arg.description: And what it is told about the gateway stream, as the argument after the payload one where a kind has both. Said by the kinds that handle gateway data -- app_gateway_veh, app_all_veh, app_all_pl -- and required of them.

vehicleType.description: The key an entry of the section groups its nodes by: the word type, one space, and the configuration's own word for the type, which is every node's under it. One of the vehicle's own: a computation, a log, a node that drops one stream, a tee that sends one stream on both ways, a node that answers pings, or a program of the vehicle's. The order of the entries, and of the nodes under each, means nothing.

payloadsType.description: The key an entry of the section groups its nodes by: the word type, one space, and the configuration's own word for the type, which is every node's under it. One of the interfaces a payload is reached over, or a payload that is a program. The order of the entries, and of the nodes under each, means nothing.

include.description: Other files this one is made of, each a subdiagram with a name of its own and the file's path from this file's directory without an extension -- zone, or ../common/zone -- read in this file's format: named rather than discovered, so the set of files a configuration is made of is itself written down.

subdiagram.description: The subdiagram's name: no node's and no other subdiagram's, with no dot or slash in it.

path.description: The file's path from this file's directory without an extension. Not an absolute path, and no part empty or ".".

exports.description: In a file another includes, what of it the files around it may join: by terminal, the nodes whose terminal of that name a line from another file may reach. A line that crosses into or out of the file at a node it does not export is refused. Not in a top file, which has nothing around it.

world-in.description: Nodes whose readings may arrive from another file.

world-out.description: Nodes whose readings may leave for another file.

moc-in.description: Nodes another file may send what the ground sends to.

moc-out.description: Nodes whose share of what the ground sends may leave for another file.

tcspecial.description: What tcspecial itself is configured with: where commands are taken, where beacons go, where the telemetry log is written. Everything optional here, because the editor has to be able to write a section somebody is halfway through filling in; what must be answered before a configuration flies is tcsverify's to say.

gateway.description: What the vehicle answers to: radio, the ground over UDP; yamcs, a Yamcs ground station over the same, every packet a CCSDS Space Packet; fprime, an F´ flight computer's bridge component, over UDP too; cfs, a cFS flight computer's software bus, as a peer of its SBN. Required, with no default; it decides how the links below are written, sockets for radio, yamcs and fprime and message IDs for cfs.

interface.description: The interface the configuration was written for: the digest of the tcslibgs/xtce/link.xtce its commands are laid out by, as 32 lower-case hex digits, which `tcsverify --interface-digest` prints. Required, and refused unless it is the build's own.

recv.description: Where tcspecial receives commands about the spacecraft and sends its responses.

send.description: Where the MOC sends them from and receives the responses.

cmd_msgid.description: On a cFS software bus, the message ID commands about the spacecraft are published under: a command's, with 0x80 set. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

response_msgid.description: And the one their answers are published under: telemetry's. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

apid.description: Where the gateway is yamcs, the APID commands on both command links carry as CCSDS telecommands, and their answers as CCSDS telemetry: 0 to 0x7FF, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x. Required there, and refused for any other gateway.

source_base.description: The MOC's end, counted on by the payload's id.

dest_base.description: tcspecial's end, counted on by the payload's id.

cmd_base.description: On a cFS software bus, the first of the message IDs node commands are published under: node k's is this plus k. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

response_base.description: And the first of their answers', counted the same way. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

source_base.description: Where a payload's telemetry leaves tcspecial, counted on by its id.

dest_base.description: Where it arrives at the ground, counted on by its id.

tlm_base.description: On a cFS software bus, the first of the message IDs a payload nothing touches is published under: payload k's is this plus k. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

apid_base.description: Where the gateway is yamcs, the first of the APIDs the telemetry of a payload nothing touches carries as CCSDS telemetry: payload k's is this plus k, at most 0x7FF. Decimal or hexadecimal with 0x. Required there, and refused for any other gateway.

default_interval.description: How often a beacon is sent once the MOC has been heard from, as a length of time: 5 s, 500 ms. It was interval, and before that interval_ms, a bare number of milliseconds.

reset_interval.description: How often a beacon is sent across a restart, as a length of time: from a restart's being initiated, and from every start until the MOC is heard from. Not nought, and no longer than interval.

send.description: The socket tcspecial sends beacons from.

recv.description: The socket tcsmoc receives them on.

tlm_msgid.description: On a cFS software bus, the message ID the beacon is published under. A cFS message ID, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x, inside msgid_range.

apid.description: Where the gateway is yamcs, the APID the beacon carries as CCSDS telemetry: 0 to 0x7FF, decimal or hexadecimal with 0x. Required there, and refused for any other gateway.

sbn.description: The SBN peer a vehicle that answers to cfs is on the software bus through. The far end's SBN table must list tcspecial with the same spacecraft_id, processor_id and address, which nothing on this side can check.

release.description: The SBN release the far end was built from, which this build must speak: v7.0.1.

ident.description: The 40 hexadecimal digits of the far end's SBN_IDENT, as SBN prints them in its start-up event.

spacecraft_id.description: The spacecraft ID SBN identifies both peers by.

processor_id.description: tcspecial's processor ID, which is not the peer's.

max_message.description: The cFS build's CFE_MISSION_SB_MAX_SB_MSG_SIZE, 32768 in cFE's example.

msgid_range.description: The block of cFS message IDs the mission allotted tcspecial, every one it uses inside it.

first.description: The first message ID of the block.

last.description: The last, which is in the block.

cfe_time.description: How the cFS build counts time, which every telemetry packet on its bus is stamped in.

epoch.description: The cFS build's epoch, a UTC date and time written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

scale.description: tai or utc, as the cFS build's CFE_MISSION_TIME_CFG_DEFAULT_TAI has it.

leap_seconds.description: TAI less UTC: stated where the scale is tai, and not where it is utc.

state_file.description: The file tcspecial keeps what must survive a restart in: which configuration the next start loads, which is confirmed, and whether the next start is commanded. On storage that survives a power cycle.

configurations.description: The directory the vehicle keeps configurations in, each under its checksum, as <checksum>.yaml or <checksum>.xml. Absent is a vehicle that keeps none, which a RESTART may restart only onto the configuration it runs.

configurations_kept.description: The fewest configurations provisioning may leave in that directory: a whole number, 1 or more, 2 where it is not stated.

load_trials.description: How many starts of the configuration the state file names may end before a matching CONNECT before it is given up for the confirmed one: a whole number, 1 or more, 3 where it is not stated. Read from the configuration on tcspecial's command line.

restart_arm_valid.description: How long a RESTART_ARM licenses a RESTART for, as a length of time: 20 min, 90 s. Twenty minutes where it is not stated; nought is refused.

payload_groups.description: Sets of payloads read on one interval, so that readings which will be compared are taken as close to together as the hardware allows.

interval.description: A number, whitespace, and a unit: 500 ms, 3 s, 1.5 s, 15 min, 6 h, 1 w. The whitespace is required and one or more characters of it will do, so 500 ms and 500  ms are the same and 500ms is refused. The units are us, ms, s, min, h, d and w, each a word of its own. Minutes are min and never m, a single m being one letter from ms and a thousand-fold apart from it; a month and a year are not units here. The number is decimal, whole or a fraction, with underscores allowed among the digits, so 1_000 ms, 1.5 s and 1500 ms are one interval written three ways. There is no hexadecimal and none is planned.

gateways.description: The ground links: what the editor's gateway working pane holds. Grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's nodes, each named by its first key, `gateway: <name>`.

vehicle.description: What the vehicle itself runs: computations, logs, pass-throughs, pages of their own. Grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's nodes, each named by its first key, `compute: <name>`.

payloads.description: What the vehicle carries this flight. Grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's nodes, each named by its first key, `payload: <name>`.

commands.description: What a named command from the ground may set, so that what the ground can change in flight is written down.

from.description: The gateway link it arrives on.

tcsgui.description: What the editor arranged: where each node was drawn. Last in the file and in a section of its own, because the sections above say what the vehicle carries and this says where somebody put the boxes on a screen. The flight software ignores it. Each entry names the node it is about by its first key, `node: <name>`, as the sections name theirs.

set-aside.description: The concerns the editor was told not to go on raising: a node, and the kind of concern somebody looked at and left.

concern.description: The editor's own word for the kind of concern.
